newsitem.title: USA: Caterpillar ordered to reinstate union official.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar ordered to reinstate union official.

text.p: Caterpillar Inc said on Wednesday it appealed a ruling ordering the company to reinstate the chairman of a United Auto Workers local who was dismissed three years ago.

On Tuesday, the National Labor Relations Board ordered Caterpillar to reinstate George Boze, chairman of UAW Local 974 in Mossville, Illinois. Boze was dismissed in December 1993 during a period of acrimonious labor relations between the union and the Peoria, Illinois-based heavy-equipment maker.

The ruling overturned a recommendation by Administrative Law Judge James Rose, who found in May, 1995, that Boze's discharge was not in violation of the law. The UAW said Boze was dismissed for protected union activities.
The ruling Tuesday also upheld a finding by Rose involving inion activity at a Denver plant.
The NLRB ruling said Cateprillar "has repeatedly engaged in numerous serious unfair labor practices..."
Caterpillar on Wednesday blasted the NLRB rulings.

"With yesterday's rulings, the board has continued its track record of reversing virtually all of Judge Rose's decisions which were in Caterpillar's favor and upholding all decisions which were against Caterpillar," Caterpillar vice president Wayne Zimmerman said in a news release.
Caterpillar shares fell 1-3/4 to 77 in New York Stock Exchange trading on Wednesday.
